oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint returns only claims permitted by the granted scopes; missing profile/email fields are expected when those scopes were not granted.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity verification should rely on sub and any actually granted claims, not assume email/profile are always present.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint accepts the user's access token, not the id_token.
oidc_jwt.note: 401 responses caused by sending an id_token are setup errors, not authorization or identity bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection returns active=true only when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can be caused by audience mismatch rather than token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Reserved scopes intentionally add audience entries or extra reserved claims to tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag these added claims/audiences as privilege escalation when they were explicitly requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange may return invalid_scope when the requested scope is invalid or exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner.
oidc_jwt.note: This is compliant narrowing behavior, not a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same valid JWT bearer assertion may succeed because the documented JWT profile grant does not describe one-time-use or jti replay tracking.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx token_endpoint JWT profile grant; claims.mdx
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay of the same JWT assertion as a freshness vulnerability without explicit replay-state documentation.

oidc_jwt.description: Invalid authorization request response_mode values are ignored and ZITADEL falls back to the default mode for the chosen response_type.
oidc_jwt.note: A changed redirect encoding mode is by design and should not be treated as inconsistent flow handling.

oidc_jwt.description: Unsupported token exchange token-type combinations are rejected according to ZITADEL's documented token-type matrix.
oidc_jwt.note: Failures from unsupported subject_token_type/requested_token_type combinations are by design.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests against /oauth/v2/token using the JWT bearer grant, the fuzzer MUST include a control login with a valid JWT alongside expired/future-token attacks. ZITADEL requires JWT bearer assertions to include aud containing the issuing domain and iat that is not older than 1 hour; otherwise login failure may be caused by malformed setup rather than exp/nbf enforcement.

For login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion MUST contain aud that includes ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss equal to the service account userId, sub equal to the same userId, exp in the future, iat within the last hour, and a kid header matching the downloaded keyId. Otherwise I1/I2 failures are indistinguishable from invalid test setup.

For private_key_jwt client authentication on /oauth/v2/token or /oauth/v2/introspect, the client_assertion MUST contain aud including ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss=sub=client_id, exp in the future, iat not older than 1 hour, and a kid header matching the application keyId. Do not interpret rejection of malformed client assertions as proof of subject-token validation.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL documents exact matching and returns invalid_grant when the redirection URI does not match the authorization request.

For I3 PKCE tests, when start_oidc_auth includes code_challenge, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier and code_challenge_method MUST be S256. ZITADEL supports only S256. A missing or wrong verifier tests PKCE binding; a different method is just unsupported setup.

For I3 state-swap tests, the fuzzer MUST track state as an opaque session-binding value across the authorization redirect and callback. ZITADEL returns the unmodified state on success and error; mismatches must be evaluated at the client/oracle layer, not by expecting a server-side identity mixup in /userinfo.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, token_exchange.audience MUST be chosen as a subset candidate of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens because ZITADEL documents that requested audience must be a subset of the combined audiences. Rejections under non-subset requests are expected behavior, not vulnerabilities.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, token_exchange.scope may be narrowed or changed, but invalid_scope can be returned when the requested scope exceeds what is granted by the resource owner. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token claims against originally authorized scope and treat invalid_scope rejection as compliant behavior.

For I5 reserved-scope audience tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud or urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud intentionally adds project IDs to the access-token audience. Do not flag added audience values as overbroad if they were explicitly requested by scope.

For I5 organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} intentionally enforces organization membership and may fail login if the user is not a member or the organization does not exist. Such failures are by design and should not be treated as generic auth instability.

For I5 token type tests on token_exchange, ZITADEL supports only the documented token-type matrix: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. The fuzzer MUST stay within this matrix when testing authorization binding, otherwise failures are expected setup errors.

For I2 replay_same_token on login_with_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability unless documentation explicitly promises one-time use. The provided ZITADEL docs describe stateless JWT bearer validation requirements but do not document jti replay tracking for JWT bearer grants.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include time claims that satisfy ZITADEL's documented rules: exp must be a Unix timestamp in the future and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use a control assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Attack variants should move exp into the past or iat sufficiently old; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed assertion construction rather than freshness enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, the assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} in docs). If aud is omitted or wrong, rejection is expected regardless of signature trust, so the fuzzer must keep aud valid while varying only the trust anchor or issuer under test.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 key-identification tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt-authenticated token/introspection calls, the JWT header MUST carry kid matching the downloaded keyId. Missing or wrong kid can cause rejection before any deeper signature/trust logic is exercised, so keep kid valid except when explicitly testing key selection behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx JWT Profile; authn-methods.mdx JWT with Private Key

oidc_jwt.constraint: replay_same_token against login_with_jwt is NOT a valid I2 vulnerability test here. The documented JWT bearer profile is a stateless assertion validation flow and the docs do not describe jti replay tracking or one-time assertion enforcement. Reuse of the same valid JWT assertion may be by design unless the platform explicitly documents nonce/jti storage for this grant.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx token_endpoint JWT profile grant; claims.mdx jti presence

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 PKCE tests using start_oidc_auth plus exchange_code_for_token, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Any other method or omitted verifier behavior may fail for configuration reasons unrelated to PKCE binding. Use S256 in the control flow, then vary only the code_verifier presence/value for attack cases.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send exactly the same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth for the control case. ZITADEL documents exact matching between authorization request and token request redirect_uri, so mismatches are expected rejections and should not be interpreted as identity confusion.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx authorization code grant; authmethods/_basic.mdx; authmethods/_pkce.mdx; authmethods/_jwtpk.mdx

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 state-swap and flow-coherence tests, start_oidc_auth should always include a distinct state value and the oracle must validate returned state at the redirect boundary. ZITADEL marks state as highly recommended for CSRF mitigation and returns it unmodified; without state, cross-session swap tests are underconstrained and results are uninterpretable.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, token_exchange audience MUST be chosen as a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens for the control case. ZITADEL documents this subset rule, so a non-subset audience is expected to fail by design and should only be used as the attack input, not the baseline.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the control token_exchange request should ask only for scopes already granted upstream. ZITADEL documents that invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds what was granted by the resource owner, so expanded-scope failures are expected enforcement, not bugs. The attack should compare exchanged token claims against original authorization intent when the request is otherwise valid.

For I5 token type tests on token_exchange, respect ZITADEL's documented token-type matrix: subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type=jwt is only meaningful with the documented combinations; user_id subject tokens require actor_token. Invalid combinations are expected setup failures, not authorization-binding violations.

For verify_granted_identity, use the access_token as the bearer credential, not the id_token. ZITADEL explicitly documents UserInfo requires the access_token of the user, and exchange_code_for_token/login_with_jwt response mapping must therefore bind session_token to access_token. Using id_token will produce false 401s unrelated to the tested invariant.

For introspect_token and revoke_session, client authentication is required by the endpoint family even though the docs summarize it as 'depending on your authorization method'. The fuzzer MUST supply either client_secret authentication or private_key_jwt credentials for a valid control request; otherwise 401 invalid_client is a setup error, not a token-validity result.

For start_oidc_auth, invalid response_mode values are ignored by ZITADEL. Do not use an invalid response_mode as an attack signal for I3 or I5 because the platform may silently fall back to the default mode for the response_type.

For reserved-scope audience and org-binding tests, some scopes intentionally modify enforcement semantics: urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces organization membership, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces membership plus username suffix, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds a project to access-token audience. The fuzzer MUST treat these scopes as policy inputs, not passive claim requests, when constructing I4/I5 scenarios.

For I4 identity comparisons, ZITADEL's UserInfo sub is an internal subject ID, not the external username or JWT sub string used in service-account assertions. The fuzzer MUST compare stable identity claims appropriate to the flow and must not expect UserInfo sub to echo the sent login identifier.

For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} / issuer domain). If aud omits the issuer domain, rejection is expected by design and cannot be attributed to signature or issuer validation behavior under test.

For I1 key-selection tests on login_with_jwt and private_key_jwt-authenticated token/introspection/revocation calls, the JWT header kid MUST be set to the downloaded keyId. Missing or wrong kid causes expected failure because ZITADEL uses kid to identify the key.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of a bug in downstream authorization binding.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, scope requested during token exchange may be rejected when it exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner; invalid_scope is documented behavior. A valid escalation test must compare exchanged-token claims/scope against the original authorization, not treat any invalid_scope rejection as a vulnerability.

For token_exchange, subject_token_type and requested_token_type are constrained by ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix. In particular, refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token or requested_token_type; jwt as subject_token is only allowed with actor_token; requested_token_type jwt yields access token as JWT; access_token requested_token_type returns opaque only. Tests using unsupported combinations will fail by design.

For I3 state_swap and other OIDC flow-coherence tests, start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token MUST preserve exact redirect_uri equality across authorize and token requests. ZITADEL documents exact redirect_uri matching; mismatches produce invalid_grant by design rather than a session-binding flaw.

For I3 PKCE tests, when code_challenge was sent at authorize time, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier and client_id. ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Any other method or missing verifier in a PKCE flow should be expected to fail by design.

For I3 request/response binding tests, start_oidc_auth should include state and nonce even though state is only recommended for code flow and nonce is mandatory for implicit flow. Omitting them weakens the oracle and can make flow-coherence failures indistinguishable from underspecified test setup.

For I5 audience tests using introspect_token, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. Therefore, active=false can mean either token invalid/revoked or introspecting client not in audience. Do not use introspection alone as the oracle for audience-binding attacks unless the introspecting client is known to be in the audience.

For I4 identity verification, verify_granted_identity via /oidc/v1/userinfo returns claims depending on granted scopes. If profile/email scopes were not granted, missing human-readable claims is by design. Use sub as the stable identity oracle, not optional profile fields.

For I5 reserved-scope tests, several ZITADEL scopes actively enforce membership or audience semantics. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces user membership in the selected organization, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces organization membership plus username suffix, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project id to access-token audience. Tests must account for these by-design scope side effects when interpreting authorization outcomes.

For I5 token_exchange claim-expansion tests, remember that userinfo and introspection claims are scope-dependent. An exchanged token lacking profile/email/resourceowner/metadata claims may simply reflect omitted scopes, while extra claims may reflect requested reserved scopes. Compare against the documented claims-by-scope matrix before flagging escalation.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API paths are relative to /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Use the correct REST gateway paths, NOT gRPC Connect paths. Proto RPC names like 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...' do NOT work as HTTP paths.
